$comment: What this LAUNCHER installs, and what a check may believe about it.
`checked` is proved against this repository by scripts/manifest-is-true.sh;
`declared` is a statement nobody can verify and carries its own `why`.
SAME QUESTION AS stack-up's MANIFEST, DIFFERENT SYNTAX, AND THAT IS WHY THE
SECOND OPINION MATTERS. estate-gates' C5 reads all three launchers from one
central file: `register <name>` out of a shell script here, compose service
keys there, Kubernetes kinds in the third. Three grammars, one parser, none
of it living where the fact lives. This is the other statement of the same
fact, made where it does.
IT SCHEDULES NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE LARGEST DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE THREE.
`schedules_routines` is empty and checked as empty, not omitted. stack-up
runs six routines on a timer and stack-k8s runs them as CronJobs; this one
installs no scheduler of any kind, so all six show up in estate-gates'
deployment-parity file as recorded gaps. Declaring the emptiness here means
the day somebody adds cron, this file has to say so rather than staying
quietly true.
THE IMAGES ARE PART OF WHAT IT INSTALLS. Unlike the other two launchers this
one BUILDS what it runs, from source it fetches, because there is no public
registry for these. Six are built by name and six more by a loop over
`<service>:<repo>` pairs, and the check reads both forms: an image added to
the loop is as invisible to a reader that only knows the explicit lines as
an undeclared component is to a central registry.
THREE PROFILES, AND TWO OF THEM ARE ALTERNATIVES. `egress` and
`egress-browser` must not both be started: compose.yaml says so in its own
comment. That is a constraint between profiles rather than a fact about any
one of them, so it is declared rather than checked.
AN OPTIONAL ADD-ON IS LISTED APART FROM WHAT `up` STARTS. `optional_addons`
names the services of the `finops` profile, the FinOps console and its
one-shot. Like `manual_jobs` they are compose services no install may start,
and manifest-is-true.sh holds the same two halves for them: a profile, and
install.sh never passing it.
distribution: git clone and ./install.sh on one machine; pins released images of every plane

manual_jobs.idryx-detect:
A TEMPLATE a person runs, not a schedule, and not by preference. Measured 2026-09-01 on the published image: `go-service.Dockerfile` builds on distroless, so there is no /bin/sh for a loop, the binary is `/usr/local/bin/service` rather than `idryx`, and `detect` has no --interval or --watch. A loop is impossible here rather than unwanted. Publishing a shell-bearing idryx would put a shell back into a governance plane to buy a scheduler, which is a security property traded for a convenience.

So it takes the shape the estate already has for exactly this: stack-k8s ships `costcrew-crew` as a suspended CronJob a person runs, and this is the compose equivalent, behind a profile no install enables. Run it with `docker compose run --rm idryx-detect`.

Verified rather than asserted: manifest-is-true.sh requires the service to exist, to sit behind a profile, and requires install.sh never to pass that profile. That is this file's answer to the `suspend: true` stack-k8s's own gate checks.

optional_addons.costcrew: The FinOps console (CostCrew), an optional add-on in the `finops` profile. Started only by hand, `docker compose --profile finops up -d costcrew`; install.sh never passes that profile and never names the service. As shipped it cannot spend: no gateway is wired to it.
optional_addons.costcrew-init: The one-shot that prepares costcrew's own volume and its one stream on the bus, in the same `finops` profile. It exists so the add-on does not have to edit init-volumes, which every install runs.

egress_and_egress_browser_are_alternativ.why: compose.yaml says it in its own comment: never both. That is a constraint between two profiles rather than a fact about either, and nothing here can check what an operator types.

init_volumes_is_not_a_plane.why: A one-shot busybox container that creates the shared volume layout and exits. It is in `installs_services` because compose starts it and this list is what compose starts; estate-gates records separately that it is not a component of the product.

three_of_the_five_and_the_other_two_are_.why:
This deployment installed NO scheduler of any kind until 2026-08-28: the planes came up and the work that keeps them producing did not happen. estate-gates recorded six divergences from 2026-08-06, on the single-box install, the one most likely to be somebody's first look at the estate.

Three run now, as loops rather than timers, because compose has no cron. The other two are not included and the reasons are facts rather than effort:
  qryx-trend scans a SOURCE TREE, and there is none in these containers; mounting the operator's disk into a governance plane to look for crypto is a bigger decision than a missing routine.
  mockryx-drill needs scenario files that live in the mockryx repository and are not in this image, and it is opt-in in both other deployments anyway.

The sixth, trailryx-seal, is the `record` profile.

trailryx_seal_runs_under_a_local_name.why: The service in the `record` profile IS trailryx-seal: the same `trailryx-node events` the other two launchers schedule, under this deployment's own name for it. stack-k8s does the same thing with five CronJobs whose names are all local. Listed under the ESTATE's name here, because that is the name the question is asked in.

vouchryx_is_off_by_default.why: @decided 2026-09-27: the launchers offer vouchryx as an opt-in delegation plane, off by default, so a gateway can verify a proved delegation chain instead of trusting a claimed one. Enabling it requires a trusted upstream issuer (VOUCHRYX_TRUSTED_ISSUERS) or an explicit, clearly-labelled demo issuer (WITH_DELEGATION_DEMO_ISSUER=1, never a production posture); install.sh refuses before anything starts if neither is given. Never published to the host: the gateway reaches it over the compose network only, and polls its revocations from there.

typed_answers_come_from_the_operator_s_c.value: TYPED_MODE=jev|own-model|off (default off); WITH_TYPED=1 alone is the stub backend
typed_answers_come_from_the_operator_s_c.why: @decided 2026-09-30: an operator chooses where typed answers come from. jev sends the fields each question names to TypeSafe's API and needs TYPED_JEV_KEY_FILE, the path of a file holding the key; own-model asks a server the operator runs and needs TYPED_MODEL_URL (ending in /v1) and TYPED_MODEL_NAME, optionally TYPED_MODEL_KEY_FILE; off installs no typryx. A key is only ever a file, copied into ./typed and mounted read only, never an environment value. jev is unpriced because no prices are wired here. Checked by scripts/typed-data-mode.sh, a statement about this repository's text and a scratch run, not about a live install.

typed_training_log_is_opt_in.value: TYPED_TRAINING=1 ./install.sh (default off); TYPRYX_TRAINING_DIR=/var/lib/typryx/training inside the typryxdata volume
typed_training_log_is_opt_in.why: @decided 2026-09-30: typryx keeps an opt-in local training log so a customer can fine-tune a model of their own on their own data. Off by default: nothing names TYPRYX_TRAINING_DIR and nothing is written. On, the directory sits in the typryxdata volume beside the ledger that holds the human truths, and `typryx export --training` (run with docker compose exec) writes only rows whose label is a human-posted truth, never a backend answer, so Jev output cannot become a training label. The data stays on the box. Needs typryx v0.3.0, which is what compose.yaml pins. Checked by scripts/typed-data-mode.sh, a statement about this repository's text and a scratch run, plus one live run on a Mac recorded in the pull request, not about a Debian install.

typed_risk_signal_is_opt_in_and_mcp_path.value: TYPED_RISK_SIGNAL=1 ./install.sh with typed answers on (default off); profile typed-risk-signal
typed_risk_signal_is_opt_in_and_mcp_path.why: @claude 2026-10-04, from the estate audit's launcher spec (its J2 design records as decided that a signal may hold a call and never deny it): typryx's wardryx-proxy puts a typed risk class (action.risk_class) on a tool call's policy decision so a hold_if_signal rule in wardryx can hold it for a person, never deny it. Off by default, refused when typed answers are off. Only the MCP broker's policy client (TOKENFUSE_WARDRYX_URL) is pointed at the proxy; the LLM gateway keeps asking wardryx directly, because a model call has no pending tool call to classify and the proxy's ask would add latency to a path with a 250 ms deadline. The proxy runs without a credential (the broker cannot send one) and is held by a network: the risk-signal network holds the proxy, the broker and wardryx, the proxy is on no other network and publishes nothing. No hold_if_signal policy is seeded. Checked by scripts/typed-risk-signal.sh, a statement about this repository's text and a scratch run, not about a live install.

the_finops_console_is_an_optional_addon.value: docker compose --profile finops up -d costcrew (profile finops, never passed by install.sh)
the_finops_console_is_an_optional_addon.why: @decided 2026-09-25 (paraphrased): an optional add-on joins the core by configuration alone and leaves the core unchanged, so a box that never enables it runs exactly what it ran without it. @claude 2026-10-07: that is why the add-on has its own one-shot (costcrew-init) rather than a line in init-volumes, why install.sh has no flag for it, and why it is published on loopback only instead of behind stack-caddy (whose single site is baked into an image in another repository). @measured `docker compose config` of origin/main's compose.yaml against this one, same fake .env, project path normalised, 2026-10-07: identical (the unused costcrewdata volume is pruned from the rendering). It runs as 10003:10003, outside the bus group, and can write exactly one file on the bus, costcrew.ndjson, which costcrew-init creates (0644, so agent-conform can read it). The file's name is the integration: genaryx keys its read offset off the stem. -stack-host is RECORD_TRUST_DOMAIN, the value record-seal is given, because trailryx takes one trust domain. -stack-passports and -stack-owner are a pair the console refuses to start without; the owner is COSTCREW_OWNER, else ALERT_TO, and with neither the console exits at start naming the owner. No -gateway is passed, so the console cannot spend; the crew runner in the same image is not started. Checked by scripts/finops-is-opt-in.sh, a statement about this repository's text and a scratch compose project, not about a Debian install.

the_chain_verifier_is_on_by_default.why: agent-stack-go#66: nothing on a box verified the hash chain of the shared bus until this. It reads every stream and appends chain_broken (high) to its own stream, agent-conform.ndjson, where heraldyx already reads. It runs as 10002:10002, outside the bus group, so the only bus file it can write is the one init-volumes gave it; its state is on its own volume. It is not an estate routine in the sense this file's schedules_routines means (it is a long-running service, like record-seal), so it is listed only in installs_services. Checked by scripts/chain-verifier-is-contained.sh.
